changes: Removed role 'owner' from Harṣu: the colophon only says the copy was written by him (liṣitaṃ ... harṣu paṃthasya, a genitive of agent). Nothing says the book was his, and there is no svapaṭhanārtham.
Titles: 'paṃtha' is kept as the brahmin surname (Panta/Pantha), and 'brāhmaṇa' is kept.
Raised confidence to high: the scribe's name is clear.
Notes expanded to cover the weekday, the stray verse and 'karmamaṃtraṃ'.

date.as_written: śrī samvat 1886 māse 2 pakṣe 2 tithau 6 vāre 2

notes: The year is written only as 'samvat 1886'. VS is assumed, matching the catalogue field and the Devanagari script with the Panta surname; this gives about 1829 CE. Month, pakṣa and weekday are given only as numbers: month 2 (probably Vaiśākha), pakṣa 2 (probably the dark half) and weekday 2 (Monday). 'liṣitaṃ' stands for likhitaṃ, and 'brāhmaṇā' probably for brāhmaṇa. 'karmamaṃtraṃ' is unclear. It may describe the text (the rite's mantras) or be a garbled epithet of the scribe, so it is not treated as a name. 'paṃtha' is read as the brahmin surname Panta/Pantha. The text after śubham ('dva viṣṇu daivatyāṃ viṣṇulokanivāsinīm | varadāṃ 5') is a stray verse fragment, probably an invocation of Gāyatrī/Sāvitrī, and contains no persons.
